raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Enable the existing PLE offload options on Ascend NPU for Qwen4-Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: - `--ple-offload-embedding` - `--ple-offload-backend pinned|file` - `--ple-offload-dir` for the file backend On NPU, both pinned and file-backed BF16 host tables are read directly through UVA by device lookup operators inside ordinary NPU graphs. Mapping failures produce explicit startup errors. Device-side prefetch remains active during graph capture. ## Modifications - Require UVA for both BF16 `pinned` and `file` backends on NPU. Query an existing mapping or register host storage with MAPPED, obtain its device pointer, construct a no-copy NPU tensor alias through the existing torch_npu AOTI C ABI, and gather with device `index_select` and TP masking. - Preserve storage lifetime, distinguish owned registrations from borrowed mappings, roll back failed setup, and synchronize before releasing owned registrations. File mappings use MAPPED only; no PINNED flag is added to turn the whole file into locked memory. - Fail during embedding construction when mapping or alias setup is unavailable. NPU PLE requires BF16 storage; FP8 is rejected before host-table allocation. - Remove CPU row selection/staging, host-ID copies, `NPUHostOffloadGraph`, and PLE-specific segmented capture from `NPUCudaGraphBackend`. Both backends use ordinary NPU graphs. - Use `get_device_module()` for PLE prefetch streams and synchronization. Enable device-side PLE prefetch inside graph capture, retaining static prefetch buffers and producer/consumer stream waits. NPU UVA needs no CPU file-prefetch worker; the existing file RSS trimmer is retained. - Keep ordinary NPU graph input-update handling and wait for the update worker before replay. - Update the existing single-device and full-model manual tests to require UVA for pinned/file, cover unsupported setup and dtype errors, and exercise the real PLE prefetch start/consume methods inside an ordinary graph. ## Accuracy Tests ### Full GPQA Diamond with UVA-only (completed 2026-10-16) **Ascend A3, BF16 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, TP8, pinned PLE enabled, ordinary NPU graphs, no speculative decoding: 181/198 correct (91.41%).** The integration source was `test/ple-with-37570` at `c831e6e773`, corresponding to this PR's PLE changes through `e13621e260`. This was a new full-dataset UVA evaluation; no predictions from the historical CPU-staging run were reused. | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Predictions and reviews | 198 each, unique indices 0–197, no missing or duplicate questions | | Accuracy | 181/198 (91.41%) | | Normal stop | 188 | | Reached 80,000-token output cap | 10; 3 scored correct and 7 incorrect | | Response errors in the completed result set | 0 | | Execution route | All eight ranks reported pinned UVA and ordinary decode-graph capture; no CPU-staging route | EvalScope 1.12.0 used thinking mode, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `max_tokens=80000`, seed 42, batch size 8, a 14,400-second request timeout, and BF16 Mamba SSM state. The 198 saved outputs contain 3,384,031 output tokens. After two service interruptions, the final attempt reused this run's own 27 completed predictions and generated the remaining 171. The accuracy table covers all 198; the final attempt's performance table covers only its 171 new requests. The initial interruption cause remains undetermined; the final resume completed without a scheduler exception. Test processes exited and the selected dies were released. The historical CPU-staging run scored 180/198 (90.91%, 5 capped responses). The UVA run is one question higher (+0.51 percentage points), with no observed aggregate score reduction. This sampling-based comparison is not a matched off/on benchmark or a proof of full token-level equivalence. All 10 capped outputs remain classified as truncated, including the three scored correct. Retained artifacts: `46_gpqa_ple_uva_20261016_summary.json`, `46_gpqa_ple_uva_20261016.final_audit.json`, and the complete prediction/review/report directory. The file tests exercised real `[40000192, 160]` BF16 shards (12.8 GB per rank), including directory reuse after server restart. No CPU-staging route or PLE graph segmentation was used. | GSM8K mode | Questions | Correct | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Normal inference, pinned PLE on | 20 | 19/20 (95%) | | MTP enabled, PLE off | 20 | 19/20 (95%) | | MTP enabled, pinned PLE on | 20 | 19/20 (95%) | The accuracy entry uses 5-shot prompts with the model chat template, thinking disabled, greedy sampling, and `max_new_tokens=1024`. Each mode generated 3,147 tokens, performed 1,613 verifications, accepted 1,522 drafts, and rejected 91 (94.36% acceptance). All 40 MTP responses stopped normally, with no empty outputs, invalid answers, or truncation; all eight target-verify graphs completed capture. These are small-sample accuracy regressions. A runner-only TCP TIME_WAIT precheck issue occurred between the functional and accuracy files; enabling SO_REUSEADDR allowed the unstarted accuracy file to continue, without changing model/test code or rerunning the passed functional files. The full UVA-only GPQA result is reported above. The earlier full GPQA result and throughput measurements below belong to the historical CPU-staging implementation. A formal matched off/on throughput comparison has not been performed for the UVA-only implementation. ### Historical CPU-staging validation (before UVA) **Test environment:** Ascend910 A3, TP8 using eight NPU dies, CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0 / torch_npu 2.10.0.post6, and triton-ascend 3.2.2. The results below refer to this tested kernel snapshot, not the current head of [sgl-kernel-npu #807](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/807). Full-model manual serving tests used local harness adjustments for an independent port, the A3 BF16 SSM flag, and an EOS-aware check of the repetitive prefill prompt. That prompt returns first-token EOS with PLE both off and on, so the check requires output token IDs and a positive completion count instead of non-empty text. Those historical file-backend results reflect the then-uncommitted harness adjustments. The current manual harness has since been revised and synchronized; its latest validation is described above. | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Existing NPU graph backend CPU unit tests | 42 passed; existing tests were not changed to accommodate the implementation | | `test/manual/ascend/test_npu_ple_offload.py` | 10 tests passed, including changed-ID replay with bitwise equality to the CPU reference | | Full-model file backend tests | 2 passed: serving and table layout | | Real-checkpoint BF16 row lookup regression | 4 tests passed; exact row equality, including TP8 shard ranges/boundaries and changed-ID replay | | PLE off/on first-token comparison, cache flushed before every request | 12/12 pairs matched chosen tokens and top-20 candidate IDs/logprobs; maximum absolute logprob difference 0 | | PLE off/on 32-token decode comparison | 8/8 paired sequences matched; 256/256 token positions and 5,120 top-20 logprobs matched, maximum absolute difference 0 | **Full GPQA Diamond, PLE pinned enabled:** **180/198 correct (90.91%)**, with 198 unique predictions and matching reviews. EvalScope 1.12.0 used thinking mode, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `max_tokens=80000`, batch size 8, and a 14,400-second request timeout. This was resumed from 82 saved predictions and completed the other 116; the accuracy report includes all 198. - 193 responses stopped normally; 5 reached the 80,000-token cap and were scored incorrect. - No response errors were recorded. - This is a PLE-only full benchmark, not a matched full-dataset off/on comparison or a reproduction of an identical published evaluation harness. - A3 requires BF16 SSM state for this checkpoint: FP32 initial state raises `FP32 initial_state is only supported on Ascend950 (arch35)`. Both sides of the paired PLE checks used BF16 state; they do not measure FP32-versus-BF16 state accuracy. - The optional graph-versus-eager exact-text test did not pass. A no-PLE control also diverged late in the continuation, and some within-mode repeat controls differed. This limits conclusions from exact-text comparisons across execution modes; the failing results were retained. They are not benchmarks of the latest UVA path.** Measured PLE off/on on the same checkpoint, TP8 devices, attention backend, BF16 SSM state, and decode graph configuration. Requests used deterministic prompts, `temperature=0`, and `ignore_eos=true` to keep output lengths equal. The helper's wait was increased to 120 seconds afterward. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. +"""NPU PLE UVA lookup for pinned and file-backed BF16 host tables.
+
+UVA is required: unsupported storage, registration, or alias APIs raise during
+embedding construction. There is no CPU staging or segmented graph fallback.
+File mappings use MAPPED only; this module never silently locks the full table.
+"""
+
+import ctypes
+import logging
+import weakref
+from functools import lru_cache
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def _acl_runtime():
+    library = ctypes.CDLL("libascendcl.so")
+    signatures = {
+        "aclrtHostGetDevicePointer": [
+            ctypes.c_void_p,
+            ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_void_p),
+            ctypes.c_uint32,
+        ],
+        "aclrtHostUnregister": [ctypes.c_void_p],
+    }
+    for name, arguments in signatures.items():
+        function = getattr(library, name)
+        function.argtypes, function.restype = arguments, ctypes.c_int
+    if hasattr(library, "aclrtHostRegisterV2"):
+        function = library.aclrtHostRegisterV2
+        function.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_uint64, ctypes.c_uint32]
+    else:
+        function = library.aclrtHostRegister
+        function.argtypes = [
+            ctypes.c_void_p,
+            ctypes.c_uint64,
+            ctypes.c_int,
+            ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_void_p),
+        ]
+    function.restype = ctypes.c_int
+    return library
+
+
+def _mapped_npu_tensor(weight, pointer, device):
+    """Wrap mapped storage through torch_npu's AOTI C ABI without copying it."""
+    import torch_npu
+
+    library = ctypes.CDLL(
+        str(Path(torch_npu.__file__).resolve().parent / "lib/libtorch_npu.so")
+    )
+    create = library.aoti_torch_create_tensor_from_blob_npu
+    dtype = library.aoti_torch_dtype_bfloat16
+    device_type = library.aoti_torch_device_type_npu
+    steal = torch._C._aoti.alloc_tensors_by_stealing_from_void_ptrs
+    for query in (dtype, device_type):
+        query.argtypes, query.restype = [], ctypes.c_int32
+    create.argtypes = [
+        ctypes.c_void_p,
+        ctypes.c_int64,
+        ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int64),
+        ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int64),
+        ctypes.c_int64,
+        ctypes.c_int32,
+        ctypes.c_int32,
+        ctypes.c_int32,
+        ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_void_p),
+    ]
+    create.restype = ctypes.c_int32
+    sizes = (ctypes.c_int64 * weight.ndim)(*weight.shape)
+    strides = (ctypes.c_int64 * weight.ndim)(*weight.stride())
+    handle = ctypes.c_void_p()
+    result = create(
+        pointer,
+        weight.ndim,
+        sizes,
+        strides,
+        0,
+        dtype(),
+        device_type(),
+        device,
+        ctypes.byref(handle),
+    )
+    if result or not handle.value:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"NPU mapped tensor creation returned {result}")
+    capsule_new = ctypes.pythonapi.PyCapsule_New
+    capsule_new.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_void_p]
+    capsule_new.restype = ctypes.py_object
+    capsule = capsule_new(handle, None, None)
+    try:
+        tensor = steal([capsule])[0]
+    except Exception:
+        delete = library.aoti_torch_delete_tensor_object
+        delete.argtypes, delete.restype = [ctypes.c_void_p], ctypes.c_int32
+        delete(handle)
+        raise
+    if tensor.data_ptr() != pointer or tensor.dtype != weight.dtype:
+        raise RuntimeError("NPU mapped tensor did not preserve storage metadata")
+    return tensor
+
+
+def _release_mapping(storage_owner, device, library, base, owned):
+    # The finalizer holds CPU storage until all uses of the non-owning NPU
+    # alias finish. Only registrations made here may be unregistered here.
+    try:
+        with torch.npu.device(device):
+            torch.npu.synchronize()
+            if owned:
+                result = library.aclrtHostUnregister(base)
+                if result:
+                    logger.warning("PLE UVA unregister returned %s", result)
+    except Exception as error:
+        logger.warning("PLE UVA cleanup failed: %s", error)
+
+
+class NpuUvaTable:
+    """Keep the alias and its registered CPU storage alive together."""
+
+    def __init__(self, weight, tensor, device, library, base, owned):
+        self.tensor = tensor
+        # Parameter attributes include a bound weight_loader pointing back to
+        # the embedding. Keep only detached storage here, or the finalizer's
+        # registry would indirectly keep its own target alive forever.
+        self._cleanup = weakref.finalize(
+            tensor, _release_mapping, weight.detach(), device, library, base, owned
+        )
+
+    def close(self):
+        """Release after callers have retired every graph using this table."""
+        self._cleanup()
+        self.tensor = None
+
+
+def create_ple_uva_table(weight: torch.Tensor, *, backend: str) -> NpuUvaTable:
+    """Register pinned/file host storage or fail before model graph capture."""
+    if backend not in ("pinned", "file"):
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid NPU PLE backend: {backend}")
+    if weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            f"NPU PLE UVA requires bfloat16 storage, got {weight.dtype}"
+        )
+    if weight.device.type != "cpu" or not weight.is_contiguous() or not weight.numel():
+        raise ValueError("NPU PLE UVA requires a nonempty contiguous CPU table")
+    if backend == "pinned" and not weight.is_pinned():
+        raise ValueError("NPU PLE pinned backend requires pinned CPU storage")
+    library, owned, base = None, False, weight.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+    try:
+        device = torch.npu.current_device()
+        library = _acl_runtime()
+        mapped = ctypes.c_void_p()
+        result = library.aclrtHostGetDevicePointer(base, ctypes.byref(mapped), 0)
+        if result or not mapped.value:
+            nbytes = weight.untyped_storage().nbytes()
+            if hasattr(library, "aclrtHostRegisterV2"):
+                # MAPPED only: do not convert the file backend into a locked
+                # whole-table allocation. Unsupported mappings must fail.
+                result = library.aclrtHostRegisterV2(base, nbytes, 0x2)
+            else:
+                result = library.aclrtHostRegister(
+                    base, nbytes, 0, ctypes.byref(mapped)
+                )
+            if result:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"host registration returned {result}")
+            owned = True
+            result = library.aclrtHostGetDevicePointer(base, ctypes.byref(mapped), 0)
+            if result or not mapped.value:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"mapped device address query returned {result}")
+        pointer = mapped.value + weight.storage_offset() * weight.element_size()
+        tensor = _mapped_npu_tensor(weight, pointer, device)
+        return NpuUvaTable(weight, tensor, device, library, base, owned)
+    except (OSError, AttributeError, RuntimeError) as error:
+        if owned:
+            result = library.aclrtHostUnregister(base)
+            if result:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"PLE UVA rollback unregister returned {result}"
+                ) from error
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"NPU PLE backend={backend} requires UVA; mapping/alias setup failed: {error}. "
+            "CPU staging is not supported; check the installed CANN, driver, "
+            "OS kernel, torch_npu APIs, and host-memory mapping support."
+        ) from error
+
+
+def gather_ple_uva_rows(table, flat_ids, output, *, vocab_start, vocab_end):
+    """Device-only row selection, TP masking, and reuse of the caller's buffer."""
+    if table.tensor is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("PLE UVA table is closed")
+    if table.tensor.device != flat_ids.device:
+        raise ValueError("PLE UVA table and IDs must use the same NPU device")
+    in_range = (flat_ids >= vocab_start) & (flat_ids < vocab_end)
+    local_ids = torch.where(in_range, flat_ids - vocab_start, 0).long()
+    rows = output.view(flat_ids.numel(), -1)
+    torch.index_select(table.tensor, 0, local_ids, out=rows)
+    rows.masked_fill_(~in_range[:, None], 0)
+    return output

+"""Single-NPU PLE pinned/file lookups against a CPU embedding reference.
+
+Run: python3 test/manual/ascend/test_npu_ple_offload.py -v
+No model weights, UVA configuration, or custom host-mapping operators needed.
+
+Progress goes to stdout with elapsed time. A test running longer than
+SGLANG_TEST_PLE_TIMEOUT_S (default 300) dumps every thread's stack and exits
+the process instead of hanging.
+"""
+
+import faulthandler
+import os
+import tempfile
+import time
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.unquant import UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod
+from sglang.srt.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+    VocabParallelEmbeddingShardIndices,
+)
+from sglang.srt.models.qwen4_exp import Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding, Qwen4ExpPLELayer
+
+# Arbitrary; every test here takes seconds when healthy.
+TIMEOUT_S = float(os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_PLE_TIMEOUT_S", "300"))
+_START = time.monotonic()
+
+
+def log(message: str) -> None:
+    print(f"[ple-test +{time.monotonic() - _START:8.2f}s] {message}", flush=True)
+
+
+class TestNpuPleOffload(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        if not torch.npu.is_available():
+            self.skipTest("NPU not available")
+        name = self._testMethodName
+        log(f"{name}: start")
+        # A hang inside C code never returns to Python, so only a watchdog helps.
+        faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(TIMEOUT_S, exit=True)
+        self.addCleanup(faulthandler.cancel_dump_traceback_later)
+        self.addCleanup(log, f"{name}: cleanup done")
+        self.device = torch.device("npu:0")
+        torch.npu.set_device(self.device)
+        directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(directory.cleanup)
+        self.directory = Path(directory.name)
+
+    def make_embedding(self, backend, dtype, dim, *, start=0, end=None, vocab=8):
+        """A host-table embedding holding rows [start, end) of a vocab-row table."""
+        end = vocab if end is None else end
+        log(
+            f"make_embedding: {backend} {dtype} dim={dim} "
+            f"rows [{start}, {end}) of {vocab}"
+        )
+        # The real constructor builds the table on meta before offloading.
+        weight = nn.Parameter(
+            torch.empty((end - start, dim), dtype=dtype, device="meta"),
+            requires_grad=False,
+        )
+        weight.output_dim = 0
+        shard = VocabParallelEmbeddingShardIndices(
+            padded_org_vocab_start_index=start,
+            padded_org_vocab_end_index=end,
+            padded_added_vocab_start_index=vocab,
+            padded_added_vocab_end_index=vocab,
+            org_vocab_start_index=start,
+            org_vocab_end_index=end,
+            added_vocab_start_index=vocab,
+            added_vocab_end_index=vocab,
+        )
+        source = SimpleNamespace(
+            weight=weight,
+            quant_config=None,
+            enable_tp=True,
+            use_attn_tp_group=False,
+            tp_size=1,
+            num_embeddings=vocab,
+            org_vocab_size=vocab,
+            padding_size=1,
+            num_added_embeddings=0,
+            use_presharded_weights=False,
+            org_vocab_size_padded=vocab,
+            num_embeddings_padded=vocab,
+            shard_indices=shard,
+            embedding_dim=dim,
+            weight_scale=torch.tensor([0.5], device=self.device),
+            quant_method=UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod(),
+            num_embeddings_per_partition=end - start,
+            num_org_embeddings_per_partition=end - start,
+            num_added_embeddings_per_partition=0,
+        )
+        table_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=self.directory))
+        embedding = Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding(
+            source, backend=backend, table_dir=str(table_dir)
+        )
+        # Keep the mapped storage alive until its background workers stop.
+        self.addCleanup(self.close_embedding, embedding)
+        log(f"  table allocated, files: {sorted(os.listdir(table_dir))}")
+        rows = (
+            ((torch.arange(vocab * dim, dtype=torch.float32) % 31 - 15) / 4)
+            .reshape(vocab, dim)
+            .to(dtype)
+        )
+        ptr = embedding.weight.data_ptr()
+        embedding.weight_loader(embedding.weight, rows)
+        log("  rows loaded")
+        self.assertEqual(embedding.weight.data_ptr(), ptr)
+        self.assertEqual(embedding.weight.device.type, "cpu")
+        self.assertEqual(embedding.weight.dtype, dtype)
+        if backend == "pinned":
+            self.assertTrue(embedding.weight.is_pinned())
+        else:
+            # is_pinned() may report registered UVA host memory as pinned.
+            # File identity and shared writes establish the backend instead.
+            filename = embedding.weight.untyped_storage().filename
+            self.assertIsNotNone(filename)
+            files = list(table_dir.iterdir())
+            self.assertEqual(len(files), 1)
+            self.assertTrue(os.path.samefile(filename, files[0]))
+        self.assertIs(embedding.weight_scale, source.weight_scale)
+        self.assertTrue(embedding.npu_uva_enabled)
+        self.assertEqual(dtype, torch.bfloat16)
+        self.assertIsNone(embedding._file_prefetcher)
+        return embedding, rows, table_dir
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def close_embedding(embedding):
+        for worker in (embedding._file_prefetcher, embedding._file_rss_trimmer):
+            if worker is not None:
+                worker.close()
+        owner = getattr(embedding, "_npu_uva_table", None)
+        if owner is not None:
+            owner.close()
+        log("  embedding workers and UVA registration closed")
+
+    def lookup(self, embedding, ids, **kwargs):
+        log(f"  gather: ids {tuple(ids.shape)} {ids.dtype}")
+        actual = embedding.gather(ids, **kwargs)
+        log("  gather returned, synchronizing")
+        torch.npu.synchronize()
+        log("  synchronized")
+        return actual
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def reference(rows, ids, start, end):
+        """bf16 rows for ids in [start, end), zeros elsewhere."""
+        ids = ids.cpu().long()
+        valid = (ids >= start) & (ids < end)
+        expected = torch.zeros((*ids.shape, rows.shape[1]), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        expected[valid] = rows.to(torch.bfloat16)[ids[valid]]
+        return expected
+
+    def check(self, actual, expected):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual.cpu(), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        log("  matches reference")
+
+    def test_pinned_and_file_gather(self):
+        for backend in ("pinned", "file"):
+            for dim in (7, 64, 257):
+                for id_dtype in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+                    with self.subTest(backend=backend, dim=dim, ids=id_dtype):
+                        embedding, rows, _ = self.make_embedding(
+                            backend, torch.bfloat16, dim
+                        )
+                        ids = torch.tensor(
+                            [[7, 0, 3], [3, 1, 6]], dtype=id_dtype, device=self.device
+                        )
+                        actual = self.lookup(embedding, ids)
+                        self.check(actual, self.reference(rows, ids, 0, 8))
+
+    def test_shard_boundaries_duplicates_and_output_buffer(self):
+        # Two disjoint TP shards without an HCCL process group; their sum is the table.
+        ids = torch.tensor([[-1, 0, 3], [4, 7, 8], [7, 4, 99]], device=self.device)
+        for backend in ("pinned", "file"):
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend):
+                combined = torch.zeros((*ids.shape, 13), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                for start, end in ((0, 4), (4, 8)):
+                    embedding, rows, _ = self.make_embedding(
+                        backend, torch.bfloat16, 13, start=start, end=end
+                    )
+                    # Keep the NaN sentinel without requiring an NPU fill kernel
+                    # just to prepare the buffer whose overwrite we are testing.
+                    log("  preparing NaN output buffer on CPU, copying to NPU")
+                    out = torch.full(
+                        (*ids.shape, 13),
+                        float("nan"),
+                        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                        device="cpu",
+                    ).to(self.device)
+                    log("  NaN output buffer ready")
+                    actual = self.lookup(embedding, ids, out=out)
+                    self.assertIs(actual, out)
+                    self.check(actual, self.reference(rows, ids, start, end))
+                    combined += actual.cpu()
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    combined, self.reference(rows, ids, 0, 8), rtol=0, atol=0
+                )
+                log("  shard sum matches the full table")
+
+    def test_file_directory_persistence_and_updated_rows(self):
+        embedding, rows, directory = self.make_embedding("file", torch.bfloat16, 13)
+        files = list(directory.iterdir())

+def expected_table_files(dtype: torch.dtype, tp_size: int) -> list[str]:
+    text_config = get_config(MODEL, trust_remote_code=True).text_config
+    ngram_heads = (text_config.ngram_size - 1) * text_config.heads_per_ngram
+    head_dim = text_config.ple_embed_dim // ngram_heads
+    divisible_by = text_config.make_ngram_vocab_size_divisible_by
+    prime = text_config.ngram_vocab_size_base - 1
+    names = []
+    for layer_id in sorted(set(text_config.ple_layer_ids)):
+        vocab = 0
+        for _ in range(ngram_heads):
+            prime = int(sympy.nextprime(prime))
+            vocab += prime
+        vocab = -(-vocab // divisible_by) * divisible_by
+        if not 1 <= layer_id <= text_config.num_hidden_layers:
+            continue
+        padded = pad_vocab_size(vocab)
+        for rank in range(tp_size):
+            shard = VocabParallelEmbedding._get_indices(
+                padded, padded, vocab, vocab, rank, tp_size
+            )
+            names.append(
+                ple_table_file_name(
+                    (padded // tp_size, head_dim),
+                    dtype,
+                    tag=f"rows{shard.org_vocab_start_index}-{shard.org_vocab_end_index}",
+                )
+            )
+    return names
+

+class TestNpuPleOffloadServer(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        if not os.path.isdir(MODEL):
+            raise FileNotFoundError(
+                f"Model weights not found in shared directory: {MODEL}"
+            )
+        cls.base_url = os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_PLE_URL", DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST)
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.process = None
+        self.owns_process_group = False
+        self.work_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ple_server_test_")
+        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.work_dir, ignore_errors=True)
+        self.table_dir = os.path.join(self.work_dir, "tables")
+        os.mkdir(self.table_dir)
+        self.cache_dir = os.path.join(self.work_dir, "cache")
+        self.observer_dir = os.path.join(self.work_dir, "observer")
+        os.mkdir(self.observer_dir)
+        Path(self.observer_dir, "sitecustomize.py").write_text(
+            RUNTIME_OBSERVER, encoding="utf-8"
+        )
+        self.stdout = io.StringIO()
+        self.stderr = io.StringIO()
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        self.stop_server()
+
+    def stop_server(self):
+        process = self.process
+        if process is None:
+            return
+        try:
+            if process.poll() is None:
+                kill_process_tree(process.pid)
+            if self.owns_process_group:
+                try:
+                    os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+                except ProcessLookupError:
+                    pass
+            process.wait(timeout=30)
+        finally:
+            self.process = None
+            self.owns_process_group = False
+
+    def common_args(self):
+        return [
+            "--trust-remote-code",
+            "--attention-backend",
+            "ascend",
+            "--tp-size",
+            TP_SIZE,
+            "--mem-fraction-static",
+            "0.85",
+            # These functional requests run singly or with four-way concurrency.
+            # Keep decode graphs enabled without capturing 52 A5 default sizes.
+            "--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode",
+            "4",
+            *EXTRA_ARGS,
+        ]
+
+    @contextlib.contextmanager
+    def isolated_cache(self):
+        # Internally isolate the default-directory test; the caller exports nothing.
+        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_CACHE_DIR": self.cache_dir}):
+            os.environ.pop("SGLANG_QWEN4_PLE_FILE_DIR", None)
+            yield
+
+    def launch(self, backend=None, *, enabled=True, table_dir=None):
+        if enabled is True and backend in (None, "pinned"):
+            ensure_pinned_memory_limit()
+        args = self.common_args()
+        if enabled is not None:
+            args += [
+                "--ple-offload-embedding" if enabled else "--no-ple-offload-embedding"
+            ]
+        if backend is not None:
+            args += ["--ple-offload-backend", backend]
+        if table_dir is not None:
+            args += ["--ple-offload-dir", table_dir]
+        self.stdout = io.StringIO()
+        self.stderr = io.StringIO()
+        env = {
+            "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join(
+                part
+                for part in (self.observer_dir, os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", ""))
+                if part
+            )
+        }
+        with self.isolated_cache():
+            self.process = popen_launch_server(
+                MODEL,
+                self.base_url,
+                timeout=SERVER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT,
+                other_args=args,
+                env=env,
+                return_stdout_stderr=(self.stdout, self.stderr),
+            )
+
+    def log(self):
+        return self.stdout.getvalue() + "\n" + self.stderr.getvalue()
+
+    def server_info(self):
+        response = requests.get(f"{self.base_url}/server_info", timeout=30)
+        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
+        return response.json()
+
+    def generate(self, prompt, *, force_decode=True):
+        params = {"temperature": 0.0, "max_new_tokens": 16}
+        if force_decode:
+            params["ignore_eos"] = True
+        response = requests.post(
+            f"{self.base_url}/generate",
+            json={"text": prompt, "sampling_params": params},
+            timeout=120,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, response.text)
+        output = response.json()
+        self.assertTrue(output["output_ids"])
+        if force_decode:
+            self.assertEqual(output["meta_info"]["completion_tokens"], 16)
+            self.assertEqual(len(output["output_ids"]), 16)
+        else:
+            self.assertGreaterEqual(output["meta_info"]["completion_tokens"], 1)
+        return output
+
+    def check_runtime_table(self, enabled, backend, directory=None):
+        records = []
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            records = [
+                json.loads(match[1])
+                for match in re.finditer(r"PLE_TEST_TABLE (\{[^\n]*\})", self.log())
+            ]
+            if records:
+                dtype = getattr(torch, records[0]["dtype"])
+                expected_count = len(expected_table_files(dtype, int(TP_SIZE)))
+                if len(records) == expected_count:
+                    break
+            time.sleep(0.1)
+        self.assertTrue(records, "No real-worker PLE table observation was recorded")
+        self.assertEqual(len(records), expected_count)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            len({(r["layer"], r["start"], r["end"]) for r in records}), expected_count
+        )
+        for record in records:
+            if enabled:
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    record["embedding_class"], "Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding"
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(record["device"], "cpu")
+                # A registered file mapping can also report is_pinned=True.
+                # Validate file storage through its real /proc/self/maps path.
+                if backend == "pinned":
+                    self.assertTrue(record["pinned"])
+                self.assertTrue(record["npu_uva_enabled"])
+                self.assertEqual(record["dtype"], "bfloat16")
+                if backend == "file":
+                    self.assertIsNotNone(record["mapping"])
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(record["mapping"])),
+                        os.path.realpath(directory),
+                    )
+                    self.assertRegex(os.path.basename(record["mapping"]), TABLE_FILE)
+            else:
+                self.assertEqual(record["embedding_class"], "VocabParallelEmbedding")
+                self.assertEqual(record["device"], "npu")
+                self.assertFalse(record["npu_uva_enabled"])
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {int(record["tp_rank"]) for record in records}, set(range(int(TP_SIZE)))
+        )
+        captures = re.findall(
+            r"TP(\d+)\].*Capture target decode NPU graph end\.", self.log()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(set(map(int, captures)), set(range(int(TP_SIZE))))
+        routes = re.findall(
+            r"TP(\d+)\].*NPU PLE lookup route: uva \(backend=(pinned|file)\)",
+            self.log(),
+        )
+        expected_routes = Counter(
+            (int(record["tp_rank"]), backend) for record in records if enabled
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            Counter((int(rank), actual_backend) for rank, actual_backend in routes),
+            expected_routes,
+        )
+
+    def check_serving(self, enabled=True, backend="pinned", directory=None):
+        info = self.server_info()
+        self.assertIs(info["ple_offload_embedding"], enabled)
+        self.assertEqual(info["ple_offload_backend"], backend)
+        self.generate("The capital of France is")
+        self.generate("Count from one to twenty: " * 64, force_decode=False)
+        self.check_runtime_table(enabled, backend, directory)
+
+    def check_table_layout(self, directory):
+        files = sorted(os.listdir(directory))
+        self.assertTrue(files)
+        dtypes = set()
+        for name in files:
+            match = TABLE_FILE.fullmatch(name)
+            self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"Unexpected table file: {name}")
+            dtypes.add(match["dtype"])
+            stat = os.stat(os.path.join(directory, name))
+            self.assertEqual(stat.st_size, int(match["nbytes"]))
+            self.assertGreater(stat.st_blocks * 512, stat.st_size // 2)
+        self.assertEqual(len(dtypes), 1)
+        expected = expected_table_files(getattr(torch, dtypes.pop()), int(TP_SIZE))
+        self.assertEqual(len(expected), len(set(expected)))
+        self.assertEqual(files, sorted(expected))
+
+    def reject_startup(self, ple_args, expected_message):
+        _, host, port = self.base_url.split(":")
+        command = [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "sglang.launch_server",
+            "--model-path",
+            MODEL,
+            *self.common_args(),
+            "--device",
+            "npu",
+            "--host",
+            host[2:],
+            "--port",
+            port,
+            *ple_args,
+        ]
+        with self.isolated_cache():
+            self.process = subprocess.Popen(
+                command,
+                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+                text=True,
+                start_new_session=True,
+            )
+        self.owns_process_group = True
+        try:
+            output, _ = self.process.communicate(timeout=180)
+            print(output, flush=True)
+            self.assertNotEqual(self.process.returncode, 0)
+            self.assertIn(expected_message, output)
+        finally:
+            self.stop_server()
+
+    def test_default_ple_switch_is_disabled_on_npu(self):

+    def test_pinned_backend_serves(self):
+        # dir must not turn pinned storage into file storage.
+        self.launch("pinned", table_dir=self.table_dir)

+        self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.table_dir), [])
+        prompts = [
+            "Explain photosynthesis.",

+    def test_file_backend_serves_and_reuses_directory(self):
+        self.launch("file", table_dir=self.table_dir)
+        self.check_serving(backend="file", directory=self.table_dir)
+        self.assertEqual(self.server_info()["ple_offload_dir"], self.table_dir)
+        self.check_table_layout(self.table_dir)

+            name: (
+                os.stat(os.path.join(self.table_dir, name)).st_ino,
+                os.stat(os.path.join(self.table_dir, name)).st_size,
+            )
+            for name in os.listdir(self.table_dir)

+        self.launch("file", table_dir=self.table_dir)
+        self.check_serving(backend="file", directory=self.table_dir)
+        self.check_table_layout(self.table_dir)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            files,
+            {
+                name: (
+                    os.stat(os.path.join(self.table_dir, name)).st_ino,
+                    os.stat(os.path.join(self.table_dir, name)).st_size,
+                )
+                for name in os.listdir(self.table_dir)

+    def test_file_backend_table_layout_and_directory_creation(self):

+    def test_incompatible_offload_arguments_rejected(self):
+        cases = [
+            (
+                ["--no-ple-offload-embedding", "--ple-offload-backend", "file"],
+                "file requires --ple-offload-embedding",
+            ),
+            (
+                ["--ple-offload-embedding", "--cpu-offload-gb", "1"],
+                "--ple-offload-embedding cannot be combined",
+            ),
+            (
+                ["--ple-offload-embedding", "--offload-group-size", "1"],
+                "--ple-offload-embedding cannot be combined",
+            ),

+                "--ple-offload-embedding",
+                "--ple-offload-backend",
+                "file",
+                "--ple-offload-dir",
